To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the biodiversity and assembly mechanisms of bacterial biofilm metacommunities within a lake system are determined by within-habitats gradients in abiotic factors, stochastic and deterministic disperser effects and biotic interactions.

(i) the biodiversity of bacterial communities in biofilms is driven by within-lake gradients in abiotic environmental conditions and by stochastic processes, (ii) the spatial variation in bacterial community composition is structured by different community assembly processes, including deterministic and stochastic dispersal and species sorting, and (iii) the spatial structure of bacterial communities within the large lake is determined to a stronger extent by abiotic environmental factors compared with biotic variables.

spatial variation in the composition of bacterial biofilm metacommunities in a large, connected lake system was structured by different community assembly processes, including dispersal limitation, stochasticity and species sorting.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the spatial structure and underlying mechanisms of bacterial biofilm community assembly within a large and connected lake system, using associative methods based taxonomic and phylogenic alpha and beta diversity and a large number and type of environmental factors.
the assembly of bacterial communities in aquatic ecosystems and their response to biotic and abiotic factors.
the spatial structure and underlying mechanisms of bacterial biofilm assembly in a highly connected lake system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial structure and underlying mechanisms of bacterial communities are highly complex and dependent on the specific environmental conditions of the studied system.
the bacterial biofilm community assembly within the lake ecosystem was driven by abiotic conditions and dispersal processes.

the spatial structure and assembly mechanisms of bacterial biofilm assemblages in the lake system are driven by within-habital gradients in abiotic factors, but also stochasticity and dispersal processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assembly of bacterial biofilms is driven by a combination of deterministic and stochastic processes and by abiotic and biotically driven mechanisms.
bacterial communities within the highly connected lake system are assembled by a complex interplay between stochasticity, deterministic processes and dispersal.

bacterial biofilm communities in a large lake ecosystem are structured by a combination of deterministic and stochastic processes and that the relative importance of each varies across spatial scales.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bacterial biofilm communities in lakes are not only structured by local environmental gradients, but also by spatially structured dispersal and assembly processes.
bacterial communities are not randomly assembled in aquatic systems, and that they can be structured by different processes depending on the spatial scale.
the spatial organization of bacterial biofilm assemblages in aquatic systems is complex and cannot be reduced simply to the influence of abiotic and/or biotic factors.
